item.title: COMIC: Temps are predicted to hit 106 in Egypt this week. How do people stay cool?
item.description: Back in the '90s, I learned the art of staying cool in Egypt. At that time, air conditioning was not common. In the extremely hot summer of 2026, how are people managing?

item.title: Some women who can't afford water are often pressured to provide sex for it
item.description: Water is often a scarce commodity in Nairobi's largest slum. The only source may be a local cartel — and with that comes the risk of sexual threats and attacks.

item.title: U.S. reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
item.description: For the second year in a row, the U.S. has reported a record-breaking number of measles cases. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday said the country has now confirmed 2,318 measles cases -- the highest case count since 1991.

item.title: 15 years later, is the FDA's produce safety overhaul working?
item.description: Fifteen years ago, the FDA overhauled its safety rules for fruits and vegetables, hoping to prevent outbreaks of foodborne illness. How's that system working today?

item.title: FDA panel backs easier access to peptides
item.description: Advisers to the Food and Drug Administration are backing popular peptide therapies. They voted to allow specialized pharmacies to make them despite agency scientists' recommendations against it.

item.title: A doctor shares how much sleep people need to function through the day
item.description: Japan's prime minister says she gets just "zero to three hours" of sleep per night. NPR's Michel Martin asks Johns Hopkins' Dr. Sara Benjamin how much sleep most people need to get through the day.
